claims.title: Verification of <byteorder_lite::LittleEndian as byteorder_lite::ByteOrder>::write_f32 (with Aeneas be86ab0f1989d04944292b345b24c435be3ad10a)
claims.precondition: Arbitrary f32 bit representation and byte slice on x86_64 with default features, under the explicit bit-pattern type and std to_bits models. Sufficient-buffer success and short-buffer panic are both specified; no floating arithmetic is modeled.
claims.report_title: Exact integer and floating bit serialization, with explicit failure conditions
claims.shared_explanation: byteorder-lite 0.1.0: fixed-width unsigned and signed integer writes, plus BE/LE write_f32/write_f64, write their exact bit representations in the selected endian order and preserve trailing bytes when the output is long enough; shorter buffers panic before writing. Float proofs quantify over every 32/64-bit representation, including NaN payloads and signed zeros, under explicit bit-pattern and std to_bits models. No floating arithmetic is modeled. The two handwritten Default methods always panic. The four variable-width unsigned writers additionally have exact byte-count/space guards, selected-byte output on success and assertion failure otherwise.
claims.shared_trusted_assumptions: F32/F64 are explicit 32/64-bit logical patterns; two executable std to_bits models preserve those patterns as unsigned words, with checked Lean value-preservation lemmas. Guards require original writer bodies and allow no other float operation. Kani checks std bit identity for every pattern and actual released writers with 6/10-byte buffers. Connecting these Rust checks to the Lean representation is reviewed, not mechanized; Rust nightlies differ. Official translation/standard integer and slice models, Lean, and Kani/CBMC are trusted. Mapped audits permit only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
claims.shared_limitations: This covers 24 selected writer methods and two handwritten Default methods, not all public APIs. Reads, remaining signed variable-width wrappers, bulk and in-place conversions, I/O extensions, other targets and release extraction remain unproved. The float result establishes bit serialization only: floating arithmetic, comparisons, rounding, numeric accuracy, NaN arithmetic and signaling behavior are not modeled. Kani public-writer buffer lengths are fixed at 6 and 10; arbitrary valid slice lengths are quantified separately by the Lean theorems. Panic messages and unwinding side effects are not specified.
